2. The short fact relevant for disposal of the Rule is that the suit property is Rowafata Rowa beel, measuring 89.99 acres ofland under Sadar Thana of Sunamganj District, originally belonged to Dewan Aftabur Reza Chowdhury Waqf Estate, subsequently Government acquired 12 annas share of the case fisheries under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950; the appellant-petitioner as Joint Mutwalli of Dewan Aftabur Reza Waqf Estate obtained the lease in the said 12 annas share of government portion in the year of 1973 corresponding to 1380 BS at a rental of Taka 3,000; since the 4 annas share of the Waqf Estate is not acquired, the CA/Roll is not finally published and thereafter the said order has been extended from time to time by the Government. Thereafter cancelled the said lease by the Memo No. SA/Char-1/95/1986 dated 5·7·1995 on the ground of non- payment of rent from 1395 as to 1401 BS The plaintiff-petitioner then filed writ petition No.1 540 of 1995 challenging the said cancellation order vide Memo No.SA/Char-1/195/1986 dated 5-7-1995 and Memo No. SA/Char-1/95/1973 (1) dated 2-7-1995 and the tender notification under notification Memo No. SA1/Chaf/1/5/95/1995(200) dated 6-7-1995 and obtained the Rule along with stay and the Deputy Commissioner, Sunamganj was directed to accept rent only for the year 1402 as from the petitioner. During the pendency of the said Rule the present petitioner filed Title Suit No,44 of 2000 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Sunamganj for declaration that the above Memo dated 5-7-1995, 2-7-1995 and 6-7-1995 were illegal, void and not binding upon the plaintiff. The High Court Division discharged the Rule by the judgment and order dated 3-11-2003; Title Suit No,44 of 2000 was also dismissed by the judgment and Decree dated 16-6-2005 passed by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Sunamganj. 

 4. Mr MA Samad, learned Senior Advocate, appearing for the petitioner, submits that the impugned judgment of the High Court Division has for all legal and practical purposes rendered the First Appeal infructuous as such, the Judgment and order is liable to be set aside; that the High Court Division has failed to appreciate the terms and tenor of the order dated 28-5-1973 of the Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reform granting lease of 12 annas share of the case Jalmohal to the appellant- petitioner till final publication of Compensation Assessment Roll in respect of the 4 annas share of the said Jalmahal which is Waqf Estate and thereby the High Court Division came to an erroneous decision, as such, caused failure of justice; that the High Court Division without considering the implication of the order dated 16-10-1996 of the Ministry of Land staying the operation of the Compensation Assessment Roll in respect of the 4 annas share of the Jalmahal comprising Waqf Estate believed the affidavit of the Deputy Attomey- General about the publication of the Compensation Assessment Roll and came to an erroneous decision that the appellant-petitioner ceased to have any interest in the 12 annas share of the Jalmahal along with the 4 annas share of the Waqf Estate; that the High Court Division erred in holding the appellant- petitioner has no subsisting interest in the 12 annas share of the Jalmahal comprising the suit Jalmahal without considering that the appellant-petitioner, being a co- sharer in the entire Jalmahal, has a preferential right to get lease of the same and the 12 annas suit Jalmahal and the 4 annas Jalmahal of the Waqf Estate are by nature and quality indivisibly connected and the said right was recognised by the Government in leasing out the suit Jalmahal by order dated 28-5-1973. 

 8. It appears from the record that in the disputed Jalmahal measuring 89.99 acres land Government has 12 annas share i.e. 66.88 acres and the rest 4 annas share belongs to Aftabur Reza Chowdhury Waqf Estate. But, in the meantime, Government acquired the rest 4 annas share and the CA Roll already published. The plaintiff-petitioner took lease of 12 annas share of the Jalmahal in 1380 BS at the rate of Taka 3,000 per year and he possessed the said Jalmahal upto 1409 BS by paying the lease money. In the meantime, the petitioner filed WP No.1540 of 1995 and obtained the Rule and the said Rule has been discharged by the judgment dated 2-11-2003. The plaintiff-petitioner filed Title Suit No.44 of 2000 before the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Sunamganj and the said suit was dismissed by the judgment and decree dated 16-6-2005. The petitioner as a lease holder possessed the said Jalmahal up to 1409 BS and his lease term had already expired and, in the meantime, the Government leased out the said Jalmahal. It is a fact that the present petitioner has no lease order after 1409 BS. The settled principle of law is that in order to get an order of temporary injunction the plantif must have a prima facie and arguable case. In this case, it is clear that the plaintiff-petitioner has no right in respect of 12 annas share since acquired and vested in the Government and for this reason an order of temporary or ad-interim injunction cannot be granted. The plaintiff has no subsisting interest in the disputed Jalmahal. The case of Md Sanu Miah vs Government of Bangladesh reported in 1 MLR (AD) 354 supports the said proposition of law.
